metric_triage_cycle_time.name: Finding Triage Cycle Time
metric_triage_cycle_time.description: Elapsed time from finding receipt to triage completion and analyst assignment. Measures the responsiveness of the intake process.

metric_risk_model_update_completeness.name: Risk Model Update Completeness
metric_risk_model_update_completeness.description: Percentage of applicable risk categories explicitly reviewed and scored during each risk model update cycle. Measures analytical thoroughness.

metric_rating_peer_deviation.name: Rating Peer Deviation Rate
metric_rating_peer_deviation.description: Percentage of proposed ratings that deviate significantly from peer group norms, requiring documented justification under the peer calibration control. Measures cross-entity consistency of risk judgement.

metric_stance_change_frequency.name: Stance Change Frequency
metric_stance_change_frequency.description: Number of entities crossing supervisory response stance boundaries per period. Measures system-level volatility in supervisory positioning — high frequency may indicate environmental stress or calibration instability.

metric_approval_cycle_time.name: Review & Approval Cycle Time
metric_approval_cycle_time.description: Elapsed time from submission of the review package to formal approval. Measures the efficiency of the governance process and identifies bottlenecks in the delegation authority chain.

metric_sap_obligation_completion_rate.name: SAP Obligation Completion Rate
metric_sap_obligation_completion_rate.description: Percentage of entity obligations from the Supervisory Action Plan completed within their specified timelines. Measures entity compliance and the effectiveness of supervisory follow-through.

metric_escalation_rate.name: Escalation Rate
metric_escalation_rate.description: Percentage of assessment cycles requiring escalation beyond the standard delegation authority (to chief supervisor or executive leadership). High rates may indicate either systemic risk elevation or delegation framework miscalibration.
